reviewed_version: Publisher version of record, retrieved 2026-10-27T10:40:58.476290+00:00; 47 pages; online 22 September 2025, printed FoCM 26 (2026), 2005–2051
paper_title: The Wonderful Geometry of the Vandermonde map
summary: Three Major proof problems are established: an invalid nonsymmetric matrix inference in Lemma 2.17, a false scaled-coordinate reduction equivalence in Theorem 6.6, and a circular connectedness argument in Lemma 2.29. A separate Minor quantifier defect in Lemma 2.28 has an exact admissible saddle witness. No main-theorem falsity is claimed.

problems.title: Positive eigenvalues do not imply positive quadratic forms
problems.location: Lemma 2.17, printed p.2019 (physical 15); uses in Lemma 2.18 p.2020 and Lemma 3.5 p.2031
problems.check: All entries and determinant 2 are positive; eigenvalues (7±sqrt(41))/2 are distinct positive, but v^T A v=-1/4 and the orthogonal compression to span(v)=-1/29. A is the actual Jacobian of (x1+x2,x1^2+x2^2) at (2,3).
problems.result: The claimed implication for totally positive matrices and arbitrary orthogonal compressions is false.
problems.counterevidence: Lemma 2.17 itself is not disproved. In the two-variable unit-weight case, ordered coordinates are recoverable from their first two moments.
problems.impact: The supplied homeomorphism proof has a missing core step used for boundary-preimage uniqueness and curved-simplex parametrizations.
problems.correction: Replace the inference with a valid injectivity/univalence argument for the ordered weighted power-sum map and verify boundary-face regularity under the full exponent/weight hypotheses.

problems.title: The reduction map omits the factors 2 and 6

assumptions.domain: Infinite probability simplex Delta with e1=1

problems.check: At the scaled uniform-four point (Y,Z)=(3/4,3/8) in R, q=-1/8192. Printed tau(q)=q(e2,e3)>=0 on all Delta because 0<=e2<1/2 and e3>=0. At uniform four, printed value is 49167625/1048576.
problems.result: Assertions (a) and (b) on p.2047 are not equivalent for the printed tau.
problems.counterevidence: The adjacent text consistently uses (2e2,6e3), strongly indicating a local omitted scaling. No undecidability theorem is refuted.
problems.impact: The explicit polynomial reduction used to transfer an undecidable problem fails as written, despite being locally repairable.
problems.correction: Use 2e2/e1^2 and 6e3/e1^3 in every group in tau. Homogenizing power 3 deg(f) still clears denominators.
problems.correction_verified: Coordinate identity verified for arbitrary f; exact witness then gives -1/8192. This does not independently reprove all cited undecidability inputs.

problems.title: Lemma 2.28 includes saddle critical points outside its stated types

assumptions.smoothness: p4=c is regular; on p2=1 the only rank-loss p4 values are 1,1/2,1/3, none equal c; boundary fiber nonempty

problems.check: Stationarity holds exactly. Multiplicity vector (1,2) is neither type (1) nor type (2). Two explicit feasible curves give lower and higher p6 values, hence a saddle.
problems.result: The all-critical-points formulation is false even under the smoothness hypotheses, after interpreting the intended domain consistently with the proof.
problems.counterevidence: This saddle is not a boundary-extremum counterexample. Restricting the assertion to local extrema is the natural repair direction; the printed Vtilde index also needs reconciliation.
problems.impact: A quantified lemma needs correction; demonstrated example alone does not damage the intended boundary classification, so severity is Minor.
problems.correction: State precisely the relevant extrema and justify the zero-coordinate cases; smooth constraint surfaces do not remove the degenerate zero-coordinate directions.
problems.correction_verified: Counterexample and two-sided saddle behavior verified. Full corrected lemma not independently proved.

problems.title: The connectedness proof ends with its own starting assumption
problems.location: Lemma 2.29 proof, printed pp.2026–2027 (physical 22–23); dependence pp.2027–2028
problems.assumptions: M is the ordered power-sum level set inside the sub-probability simplex, as defined in the source.
problems.check: The proof starts by assuming M disconnected, obtains connected p1-level slices, and ends by concluding M disconnected as a purported contradiction. No established connected ambient set or interval property of the attainable p1 values closes the argument.
problems.result: The displayed proof does not establish Lemma 2.29.
problems.counterevidence: No counterexample to the Vandermonde connectedness statement is asserted. A generic disconnected compact union of two line segments with singleton nonempty slices only illustrates why the supplied slice argument is logically insufficient.
problems.impact: Connectedness is explicitly needed in Lemma 2.31 for unique boundary preimages, then Lemma 2.32 and Theorem 2.27, with subsequent limiting geometry depending on it.
problems.correction: Supply an independent proof that the attainable p1-range is an interval (or another valid connectedness argument), covering singular values; combine compactness and connected fibers correctly. Merely replacing the final word is insufficient.

limitations: Complete page reading is not a complete independent verification of every proof.
No claims that main geometry or undecidability theorems are false; three Major findings concern invalid or incomplete central derivations.
Minor P3 disproves only an overbroad all-critical-points assertion; its saddle does not refute the intended boundary-extremum classification.
Historical initial-review status: No independent acceptance or human adjudication. Current independent acceptance is recorded separately in provenance; human adjudication remains pending.
